Consult Summary:
- Postpartum patient (4 weeks after Cesarean) with acute shortness of breath and new cough; concern for thromboembolic disease; advised urgent hospital evaluation; patient will self-transport with baby; avoid Codeine en route; Ibuprofen allergy documented.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Shortness of breath starting about 1 hour ago while resting (watching TV); new cough starting yesterday; no chest pain reported; chest feels sore on very deep breath; patient perceives heart racing.
- Time course: SOB began within the last hour, at rest; cough began yesterday; no prior similar episodes reported.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: None described.
- Associated symptoms: Chest soreness with deep inspiration; postpartum status (Cesarean delivery 4 weeks ago); baby is with patient; no fever reported.
- Past Medical History: No chronic medical conditions documented aside from recent Cesarean delivery; allergies: Ibuprofen.
- Medications: Postpartum analgesia included Codeine; patient has been taking Codeine fairly regularly but not within the last week; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Social History: Living with baby; partner at work; no one else at home; patient will go to hospital with baby; no information provided on smoking/alcohol use.
- Family History: Mother has history of clots in legs (DVT).

Past Medical History (summary):
- Medical conditions: None documented aside from recent pregnancy/postpartum status.
- Allergies: Ibuprofen.
- Medications: Codeine (dose/route/frequency not documented); more recent use not specified.

Social History:
- Partner at work; patient alone at home with infant; planning to go to hospital with baby; no other social details provided.

Family History:
- Mother with history of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in legs.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented in formal exam; patient attempted to measure pulse.
- Exam findings: Shortness of breath noted; chest soreness on deep inspiration; C-section scar tenderness described.
- Heart rate: Patient counted 30 beats in 60 seconds; clinician stated the heart is “running slightly fast” at the moment. This is a conflicting finding.

Investigations:
- None performed or documented at the time of this encounter.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Possible postpartum thromboembolism (DVT/PE) given recent Cesarean delivery and acute shortness of breath.
  - Plan:
    - Recommend urgent hospital evaluation for cardiopulmonary assessment and possible imaging/labs.
    - Discussed two transport options: call an ambulance or self-transport to hospital with baby; patient elected to self-transport.
    - Advise bringing the baby and minimal belongings; avoid taking Codeine during transport.
- Issue 2: Discrepancy in heart rate assessment.
  - Plan:
    - Acknowledge conflicting HR data (patient’s 30 bpm reading vs clinician’s note of tachycardia) and prioritize hospital evaluation to assess rhythm and hemodynamics.
- Issue 3: Medication/allergy considerations.
  - Plan:
    - Document ibuprofen allergy; avoid NSAIDs.
    - Review Codeine use; advise not to take Codeine while awaiting evaluation (dose/route/frequency not documented in current context).

General plan:
- Proceed with emergency evaluation at a hospital promptly; if clot confirmed or suspected, hospital management will follow standard protocols (not specified in transcript).

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Formal vital signs (office/lab values) and complete physical examination details.
  - Comprehensive review of systems beyond SOB and cough.
  - Medication reconciliation (current meds list with doses, routes, frequencies; including any anticoagulants if applicable).
  - Documentation of obstetric follow-up or postpartum status beyond Cesarean date.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Heart rate data conflict: patient palpated 30 bpm; clinician described the heart as running slightly fast.
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally coherent; some repetition and informal phrasing; missing some standard exam elements due to telecommunication and crisis-led conversation.
